Un programa de formación práctica y desa: An AEMCiCD program for hands-on learning and technology development. Students design, build and document electronic refreshable Braille prototypes, with attention to repairability and the involvement of people with visual impairments.
Formación técnica vinculada con una nece: Technical learning connected to an accessibility need
El Braille representa caracteres mediant: Braille represents characters through combinations of raised dots. A refreshable cell changes the position of those dots electronically. Building a prototype requires combining mechanics, electronics and programming, as well as understanding how a person explores the dots through touch.
BrailleLab propone convertir ese desafío: BrailleLab turns this challenge into a collaborative learning experience. Teams should understand and document their design decisions so that others can review, repair or continue their work. User involvement guides evaluation of the solutions.
El programa contribuye a los fines acadé: The program contributes to AEMCiCD's academic and social purposes by connecting scientific learning, student cooperation and technology with a social purpose. Open design aims to share knowledge and support the continued development of prototypes.
Personas interesadas en aprender mediant: People interested in learning through prototype design. The work combines electronics, programming, mechanical design, documentation and collaboration. Each edition sets its participation requirements and deliverables.
Personas con discapacidad visual y organ: People with visual impairments and organizations that can contribute their experience to identifying needs and validation. Their participation helps assess whether technical decisions fit the intended use.
Docentes, profesionales y organizaciones: Faculty, professionals and organizations that can support learning, technical review or materials. The scope of each collaboration is coordinated with the program team.
La edición 2027 se coorganiza con la Ram: The 2027 edition is co-organized with the IEEE Yachay Tech Student Branch. The challenge is to design and build an electronically controlled, documented six-dot refreshable Braille cell. The planned process combines training, prototyping and a final presentation.
